reply:
Yes — if your qualifying income was more than £50,000 for 2024-25, you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2026. Qualifying income means self-employment and property income before expenses (turnover/gross), not profit.

Official guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/find-out-if-and-when-you-need-to-use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax

sources.title: MTD Income Tax £50,000 threshold starts 6 April 2026
sources.excerpt: If your qualifying income was more than £50,000 for the 2024-25 tax year (2024 to 2025), you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2026. Qualifying income is total self-employment and property income before expenses (turnover/gross), not profit. Do not confuse this £50,000 / April 2026 band with the later £30,000 / April 2027 band.

sources.title: Who needs Making Tax Digital for Income Tax and when
sources.excerpt: You need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax if you are a sole trader or landlord registered for Self Assessment, you get income from self-employment or property (or both), and your qualifying income is more than the relevant threshold. Start dates depend on qualifying income in a prior tax year: more than £50,000 for 2024-25 means from 6 April 2026; more than £30,000 for 2025-26 means from 6 April 2027; more than £20,000 for 2026-27 means from 6 April 2028. Partnerships will be brought in later. Always confirm on GOV.UK.

sources.title: MTD Income Tax £30,000 threshold starts 6 April 2027
sources.excerpt: If your qualifying income is more than £30,000 for the 2025-26 tax year (2025 to 2026), you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2027. This is not April 2026. April 2026 applies only to the higher £50,000 qualifying-income band (based on 2024-25). Qualifying income is turnover/gross self-employment and property income before expenses, not profit after expenses.
